title: Not all freight indices are created equal
snippet: Read partially: the page returned navigation and a truncated body, so the advisory's own text was not obtained. Its substance reached me through trade-press quotation instead — that the SCFI explicitly includes BAF, FAF and other seaborne surcharges in its cumulative rate calculation, and that indices do not all treat those components the same way, creating unintended exposure where the index does not reflect the cost structure the parties contemplated. This is a law firm client advisory, so it is analysis rather than data, and it publishes no cost comparison.

title: Index-linked shippers warn carriers over 'double-dipping' on emergency BAFs
snippet: Read in full. Trade press on the surcharge-composition dispute: shippers arguing that an emergency BAF cannot be levied on top of an index-linked rate when the index already contains fuel components. Quotes the HFW advisory and a Xeneta analyst on the same point. Directional and contractual rather than arithmetical — no per-container figures and no comparison of composite against lane movement.

title: Shanghai Shipping Exchange, freight index methodology and FAQ
snippet: Read in full, and it is a primary source. Defines SCFI individual route rates as the average all-in price covering spot ocean freight and related seaborne surcharges, listing BAF, FAF, LSS, EBS, EBA, CAF, YAS, PSS, WRS, PCS and canal fees, and excluding landside items such as terminal handling and inland on-carriage. States that the SCFI composite is a weighted average of fifteen routes targeting Shanghai export spot rates, while the CCFI targets national export container transport including contractual as well as spot rates. It does not define whether CCFI route rates are equally all-in, which is the gap our article flags rather than fills.
